# Poland TRAVEL SURVIVAL KIT

**Traveler Types Covered**: Budget/Luxury/Family/Solo

## 1. SIM CARD SOLUTIONS

**Purpose**: Access Poland’s high-speed 4G/5G networks, which are among the most affordable in Europe.

| **Aspect**            | **Details to Find**                                                         |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Providers**         | Orange, Play, T-Mobile, Plus                                             |
| **Price Options**     | 5 PLN (Starter), 30 PLN (30GB/month), 50 PLN (100GB/month) |
| **Data Allocation**   | Generous; usually 10GB to 200GB depending on the "top-up" promotion |
| **Validity Period**   | 7 to 30 days for most prepaid starters |
| **Hotspot/Tethering** | Allowed on all major networks |
| **Coverage**          | Excellent nationwide; 5G prevalent in major cities like Warsaw, Kraków, and Wrocław |
| **Where to Buy**      | Żabka convenience stores, Relay kiosks, airport newsstands, official carrier stores |
| **Alternative: eSIM** | Airalo (starts ~4.50 USD), Holafly (Unlimited data from ~19 USD) |

**Recommendations Framework**
- **Short trips (3-7 days):** Buy an Orange or Play "Starter" for 5 PLN at any Żabka and top up for 10-20 PLN.
- **Staying 1 month:** T-Mobile or Orange monthly prepaid plans (30-40 PLN) offer massive data bonuses.
- **Digital Nomads:** Orange Flex (app-based) offers the most flexibility and large data buckets.

---

## 2. AIRPORT TRANSFERS

**Route**: From Warsaw Chopin (WAW) to Warsaw City Center (Warszawa Centralna)

| **Mode**                     | **Duration**       | **Cost**      | **Booking**                    | **Convenience** | **Best For**               |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------- | -------------------------- |
| **SKM/KM Train**             | 20–25 mins         | 4.40 PLN      | Machine on platform/app        | Excellent       | Speed and value            |
| **Bus (175)**                | 30–45 mins         | 4.40 PLN      | Machine on bus/stop            | Good            | Direct to Old Town area    |
| **Ride-hailing (Uber/Bolt)** | 20–40 mins         | 30–60 PLN     | App-based                      | Very Good       | Door-to-door convenience   |
| **Taxi (Licenced)**          | 20–30 mins         | 40–70 PLN     | Taxi rank outside arrivals     | Good            | Business travelers         |

**Detail Each Option**
- **SKM/KM Train:** Lines S2 or S3. Board at the underground station connected to Terminal A. Tickets can be bought via the "Jakdojade" app or machines (select 20-minute or 75-minute Zone 1 ticket).
- **Ride-hailing:** Follow "Bolt/Uber" signs to the specific pickup zone (usually at the departures level or a designated area). 
- **Operating Hours:** Trains run roughly from 05:00 to 23:30. Night bus N32 operates after midnight.

## 3. CURRENCY EXCHANGE

**Current Exchange Rate**: 1 USD ≈ 4.00 PLN (Polish Złoty)

#### Best Exchange Locations
| **Location**        | **Why It's Best**          | **Address**  | **Hours**       | **Rates**       | **Tips** |
| ------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------ | --------------- | --------------- | -------- |
| **Tavex** | Excellent rates, transparent | Świętokrzyska 32, Warsaw | 09:00 - 20:00 | Mid-market | Best for large sums |
| **Kantor Conti** | Famous for fair rates | Chmielna 26, Warsaw | 09:00 - 22:00 | Competitive | Located near city center |
| **Kantor Apollo** | Reliable in Kraków | Starowiślna 4, Kraków | 08:00 - 22:00 | High-tier | Avoid the Main Square booths |

**Universal Tips**
- Avoid "Interchange" or airport booths; they can be 20% worse than city rates.
- Always look for the word **KANTOR**. 
- Poland is highly cashless; you can pay by card/phone almost everywhere, including small kiosks.

## 5. MUST-TRY FOODS

🍽️ **Pierogi – Dumplings**
- **What**: Dough pockets filled with meat, cheese/potato (Ruskie), or fruit.
- **Where**: Pierogarnia chains or "Zapiecek."
- **Price**: 25–40 PLN.

🍽️ **Żurek – Sour Rye Soup**
- **What**: Fermented rye flour soup with white sausage and boiled egg.
- **Where**: Traditional Polish restaurants (e.g., Stary Dom).
- **Try with**: Served in a hollowed-out bread bowl.

🍽️ **Zapiekanka – Polish Pizza**
- **What**: Open-faced baguette with mushrooms, cheese, and ketchup.
- **Where**: Kazimierz district (Plac Nowy) in Kraków.
- **Price**: 15–25 PLN.

## 7. SUPERMARKETS & CONVENIENCE STORES

- **Biedronka**: The most popular discount supermarket. Best for cheap groceries and snacks.
- **Żabka**: Found on every corner. Best for coffee, hot dogs, and quick essentials. Open late.
- **Rossmann**: The go-to for toiletries, medicine (basic), and cosmetics.
- **Auchan/Carrefour**: Massive hypermarkets for clothing and electronics.

## BONUS SECTIONS

### 11. LOCAL CUSTOMS & ETIQUETTE

#### 11a. Temple & Sacred Site Dress Code
Poland is predominantly Catholic, and churches are active places of worship requiring respectful attire.

| **Rule**                | **What to Check**                            | **Enforcement Level**           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **Shoulders covered**   | Recommended inside churches                  | Moderate                        |
| **Knees covered**       | Preferred in cathedrals                      | Moderate                        |
| **Footwear**            | Keep shoes on                                | Standard                        |
| **Hat removal**         | Men must remove hats                         | High                            |

#### 11b. Personal Space & Greetings
Greetings are usually formal with a firm handshake and direct eye contact. Poles value personal space and appreciate a polite "Dzień dobry" (Good day) when entering shops.

#### 11c. Clergy Interactions & Religious Etiquette
Priests and nuns are highly respected members of society. Avoid interrupting masses for sightseeing and refrain from photography during active services.

#### 11d. Saving Face & Social Directness
Poles are often very direct and may appear blunt compared to Western standards. This honesty is not intended as rudeness but as a sign of sincerity and transparency.

#### 11e. Responsible Tourism
Support local "Milk Bars" (Bar Mleczny) for affordable, authentic food that preserves Polish culinary history. Always recycle, as Poland has strict waste segregation laws.

#### 11f. General Social Customs
Remove your shoes when entering someone's home unless told otherwise. Tipping is customary at 10-15% in restaurants for good service.

---

### 12. SAFETY & PRACTICAL INFORMATION

#### 12a. Vaccinations & Preventative Health
Standard European health requirements apply to Poland.

| **Vaccine / Medication**           | **Priority Level**   | **Notes**                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Tick-borne Encephalitis**        | Destination-specific | Recommended for hikers in forested areas                                                            |
| **Hepatitis A/B**                  | Standard             | General travel precaution                                                                           |
| **Tetanus**                        | Recommended          | Ensure booster is current                                                                           |

#### 12b. Mosquito-Borne Illness & Seasonal Pests
Ticks are the primary concern in Polish forests and parks during summer. Use repellent and check for ticks after walking in tall grass to prevent Lyme disease.

#### 12c. Water & Food Safety
Tap water in major Polish cities is safe to drink and of high quality. Food hygiene standards are strictly regulated by EU law, making street food and restaurants generally safe.

#### 12d. Personal Safety & Crime Awareness
Poland is consistently ranked as one of the safest countries in Europe for tourists. Violent crime is extremely rare, but standard urban precautions should be taken.

**ISSUE: Pickpocketing**  
**WHERE IT HAPPENS:** Crowded tourist areas like Warsaw’s Old Town, Kraków’s Main Square, and public transport (especially the 175 bus to the airport).  
**HOW IT HAPPENS:** Usually in crowded situations or through "distraction" techniques in busy squares.  
**HOW TO AVOID IT:** Keep your valuables in zipped pockets or bags worn in front. Never leave your phone on a restaurant table.  
**WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS:** Report the theft to the nearest Police station (Policja) to get a report for insurance.

**ISSUE: Strip Club Scams**  
**WHERE IT HAPPENS:** Major nightlife areas in Kraków, Warsaw, and Wrocław.  
**HOW IT HAPPENS:** Promoters offer "free entry" or "cheap drinks." Once inside, customers are charged exorbitant prices for drinks or have their cards charged multiple times while "intoxicated."  
**HOW TO AVOID IT:** Avoid all strip clubs promoted on the street. If a promoter is overly aggressive, walk away. Only visit established, well-reviewed nightlife venues.  
**WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS:** If you suspect fraud, contact your bank immediately to freeze your card and report it to the police.

#### 12e. Emergency Contacts
| **Service**                            | **Contact**                     | **Notes**                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| **European Emergency No.**             | 112                             | All services (English speakers available)       |
| **Police**                             | 997                             | Direct line                                    |
| **Ambulance**                          | 999                             | Direct line                                    |
| **US Embassy (Warsaw)**                | +48 22 504 2000                 | Al. Ujazdowskie 29/31                          |

### 13. SEASONAL CONSIDERATIONS
Winter (Dec-Feb) can be very cold (-10°C) but offers beautiful Christmas markets. Summer (June-Aug) is mild and perfect for festivals, though popular cities become very crowded.

### 14. GENERAL TIPS
- **Sunday Trading Ban**: Most supermarkets and shops are closed on Sundays. Plan your shopping for Saturday.
- **Public Toilets**: Often cost 2-5 PLN; keep small change or use "Żabka" or malls.
- **Power Sockets**: Type E/F (standard European 2-pin), 230V.
